speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these balance and coordination issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms of appearing "drunk" and clumsiness on the right side suggest cerebellar involvement; could you tell me if these symptoms came on suddenly or developed gradually?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain (Cerebellum)
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI confirms multifocal demyelinating lesions in the cerebellum consistent with PML, which explains your progressive gait and limb ataxia. Given this is an opportunistic infection, I need to know immediately if you are currently HIV-positive or have received immunosuppressive therapy like rituximab.
